nodes.name: Sol-gel liquogel formation
nodes.procedure: 100 mg of RuCl3·3H2O and 26 mg of CrCl3·6H2O were mixed with 10 mL of ethanol to form a homogeneous solution. 10 mL of 1 M C6H8O7·H2O in ethanol was added dropwise into the solution under vigorous stirring. The solution was then aged overnight and dried at 120 °C to produce a brown liquogel.

nodes.name: Acid leaching and purification
nodes.procedure: After cooling to room temperature, the powder was careful grinded and immersed in 1 M HCl for 12 h. Finally, the sample was washed three times with ethanol and deionized water, respectively, and dried in vacuum at 60 °C to obtain Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x.

nodes.description: OER performance in 0.1 M HClO4 using RDE
nodes.source_text: The OER catalytic activity of Cr_{0.2}Ru_{0.8}O_{2·x} was assessed using the rotating disk electrode (RDE) method in 0.1 M HClO4. Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) of Cr_{0.2}Ru_{0.8}O_{2·x} exhibits an overpotential of 170±6 mV at 10 mA cm^{-2} (Fig. 3a)... The Tafel slope of Cr_{0.2}Ru_{0.8}O_{2·x} in the second region was 75.3 mV dec^{-1} (Fig. 3b)... Cr_{0.2}Ru_{0.8}O_{2·x} exhibits the largest ECSA (220.3 cm²)... representing an average Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 99.8±0.3%

nodes.description: OER chronopotentiometry stability at 10 mA/cm² in 0.1 M HClO4 on carbon paper
nodes.source_text: the chronopotentiometry (CP) curves of Cr_{0.2}Ru_{0.8}O_{2·x} shows that the overpotential at 10 mA cm^{-2} increased 26 mV after 2000 h (Fig. 3e), representing a degradation rate of 13 μV h^{-1}. ... the concentrations of Ru and Cr in the electrolyte were 168 and 91 ppb after 2000 h stability test, corresponding to the mass loss of ~1.67% with Ru and -7.79% with Cr over their stoichiometric loadings

In a practical PEMWE device, Cr_{0.2}Ru_{0.8}O_{2·x} exhibits durability of over 200 h at 1 A cm^{-2} and 60°C... Cr_{0.2}Ru_{0.8}O_{2·x} requires a cell voltage of 1.77 V at 1 A cm^{-2}, which is 260 mV lower than that of commercial RuO2... can be operated steadily at 1 A cm^{-2} over 200 h, with potential increase of only 64 mV (Fig. 3g)

nodes.description: OER accelerated degradation test (ADT) in 0.1 M HClO4
nodes.source_text: we further investigated the acidic OER stability of Cr_{0.2}Ru_{0.8}O_{2·x} by employing the accelerated degradation tests (ADT). After 5000 cycles, the LSV curve of Cr_{0.2}Ru_{0.8}O_{2·x} experienced a minor shift, with the overpotential at 10 mA cm^{-2} increased by mere 5 mV

nodes.source_text: At a higher current density of 100 mA cm^{-2}, Cr_{0.2}Ru_{0.8}O_{2·x} also demonstrated superior stability with an additional overpotential of 96 mV for over 300 h

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x shows rutile-structured RuO2 crystalline phase without phase segregation; diffraction peaks shift to higher angles indicating lattice contraction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 1b, the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern shows that the crystalline phase of Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x matched the rutile-structured RuO2 without phase segregation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x, homemade RuO2, and commercial RuO2 show characteristic Raman peaks at 521, 638, and 705 cm⁻¹ corresponding to Ru-O vibrational modes Eg, A1g, and B2g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x, homemade RuO2, and commercial RuO2 present the same characteristic Raman peaks at 521, 638, and 705 cm⁻¹, corresponding to the Ru-O vibrational modes of Eg, A1g, and B2g, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x shows interconnected uniformly sized nanoparticles with average diameter ~6.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) ... images of Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x clearly show an interconnected and uniformly sized nanoparticles morphology with an average diameter of ~6.5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x nanoparticles exhibit good crystallinity with well-resolved lattice fringes corresponding to (110) planes of rutile RuO2, testifying lattice contraction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Each nanoparticle exhibits good crystallinity and well-resolved lattice fringes corresponding to the (110) planes of rutile RuO2, testifying the lattice contraction caused by the incorporation of Cr.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping displays homogenous distribution of Ru, Cr, and O elements throughout Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive spectroscopic (EDS) mapping images display the homogenous distribution of Ru, Cr, and O elements throughout the catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x nanoparticles possess Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 40.0 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) adsorption/desorption isotherms disclose that the Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x nanoparticles possess a relatively high surface area of 40.0 m² g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS determines overall Ru percentages and Cr/Ru mole ratios of different catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The overall Ru percentages and Cr/Ru mole ratios of different catalysts were further determined by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x shows Cr 2p3/2 peaks at 576.0 eV (Cr³⁺·O) and 577.9 eV (Cr³⁺·OH); Ru 3p3/2 peaks at 463.1 eV (Ru⁴⁺) and 465.1 eV (Ru³⁺) with lower Ru⁴⁺/Ru³⁺ ratio vs homemade RuO2; O 1s peaks at 529.8 eV (OL), 531.1 eV (Ov), 533.0 eV (OHad) with increased Ov/OL ratio after Cr doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a shows the doublet peaks of Cr 2p3/2 and 2p1/2 orbitals of Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x. The Cr 2p3/2 spectrum could be fitted with the peaks at 576.0 and 577.9 eV, ascribable to Cr³⁺·O and Cr³⁺·OH. For Ru 3p3/2, the fitted peaks at 463.1 and 465.1 eV could be assigned to Ru⁴⁺ and Ru³⁺, respectively ... the O 1s spectrum of Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x could be deconvoluted into three peaks located at 529.8, 531.1, and 533.0 eV, corresponding to lattice oxygen (OL), oxygen vacancies (Ov), and surface-adsorbed hydroxyl species (OHad), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows absorption edge slightly shifted to lower energy than commercial RuO2 indicating lower Ru oxidation state; FT-EXAFS shows Ru-O peak at ~1.50 Å with coordination number 5.67 due to oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absorption edge of Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x was found to be slightly shifted to lower energy compared with that of commercial RuO2 ... Quantitative FT-EXAFS fitting yielded a Ru coordination number of 5.67.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr K-edge XANES shows Cr oxidation state close to +3 of Cr2O3; distinct FT-EXAFS indicates Cr incorporation inside RuO2 lattice without Cr2O3 or Cr metal nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the oxidation state of Cr in Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x was very close to Cr2O3 of +3 ... the distinct FT-EXAFS spectrum compared with that of the Cr2O3 or Cr reference revealed that no obvious Cr2O3 or Cr metal nanoparticles were formed.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR confirms higher oxygen vacancy concentration in Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x compared with homemade RuO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra confirmed the higher Ov concentration in Cr0.2Ru0.8O2·x compared with that in homemade RuO2.
